chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ṣabbāḥ ibn Sayyābah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said:

Whichever muʾmin or Muslim dies and leaves a debt that was not incurred in corruption nor extravagance, then it is upon the Imam to discharge it. If he does not discharge it, then the sin of that is upon him.
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: “The charities are only for the poor and the needy...” — the verse.
So he is among the debtors, and he has a share with the Imam. If he withholds it, then its sin is upon him.

key_terms.إِثْمُهُ: Its sin; the liability for withholding the rightful payment.
key_terms.إِسْرَافٍ: Extravagance or wasteful excess that would disqualify the debt from this support.
key_terms.الصَّدَقَاتُ: Charitable funds mentioned in the Quran as allocated to designated recipients.
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The Imam, who bears responsibility for discharging such eligible debts.
key_terms.الْغَارِمِينَ: Those burdened by debt and thus entitled to a share from charitable funds.
key_terms.دَيْنًا: A financial debt left by the deceased.
key_terms.سَهْمٌ: An allotted portion or share due from the Imam’s public funds.
key_terms.فَسَادٍ: Corrupt or wrongful conduct through which debt may be incurred.

ai.seo_question: Is the Imam responsible for paying the legitimate debts of a deceased believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a muʾmin or Muslim dies leaving a legitimate debt not caused by فساد or extravagance, the Imam is responsible for settling it. It grounds this responsibility in the Quranic category of الغارمين, showing that public religious funds include support for debtors and that withholding such due support carries sin.
